title: Standardize pricing experiment success metrics + stop criteria (with Finance approval workflow)
creator: Nikhil Sharma
description:
## Context
We have multiple Q1 pricing/packaging experiments in flight and an ongoing metering hardening effort. Readouts have been inconsistent across teams (different denominators, different retention windows, some analyses mixing pre/post meter fixes). This ticket standardizes:
- Success metrics (conversion, retention, ARPU, margin)
- Stop/continue criteria + guardrails
- A Finance approval workflow so we don’t ship/scale experiments with incomplete RevRec/margin implications

This should be the single internal source that Product Ops, PMs, and RevOps use to evaluate experiments and make scale/stop decisions.

## Goals / deliverables
1) **Metric dictionary** for pricing experiments (primary + secondary metrics) with exact definitions and recommended reporting cuts.
2) **Standard stop criteria** (statistical + business guardrails) with clear owners.
3) **Readout template** (1-pager) with required sections and caveat callouts (esp. meter changes).
4) **Approval workflow** with Finance/RevRec for:
   - Launching a new variant
   - Increasing rollout %
   - Concluding experiment + making pricing changes durable

## Scope
Applies to:
- Hosted API self-serve pricing/packaging variants (free tier, included usage, overage behavior)
- Sales-assisted discounts/credits when tied to experiment exposure (must be tracked and included in analysis)
- Dedicated add-ons ONLY to the extent they are part of packaging experiments (Dedicated GPU-seconds meter definitions handled separately)

Out of scope:
- Pure product experiments not affecting price/packaging
- One-off enterprise deal desk exceptions not tied to a cohort flag (but we should tag them as exclusions)

## Standard definitions (v1)
### Units
- **Account** is primary unit for conversion/retention metrics.
- **Workspace/Project** rollups allowed as secondary views but must not be the only view.
- **Seat/user** is not a primary unit for now.

### Primary success metrics (must be in every readout)
1) **Net Revenue Retention (NRR) – 60 day (early)**
   - Definition: (Revenue from cohort accounts in days 31–60) / (Revenue from same accounts in days 1–30)
   - Cohort: accounts active at least once in days 1–7 post exposure
   - Notes: use billed usage dollars from billing ledger; credits applied should be reflected as revenue offsets per Finance guidance.

2) **Paid conversion – 14 day**
   - For self-serve: % of new signups that cross the paywall / add payment method and generate >$X billed usage within 14 days of exposure.
   - Default threshold: >$5 billed usage (to avoid noise from tiny accounts). Adjust per variant if paywall rules change.

3) **Gross margin impact (contribution margin) – blended**
   - Definition: (Usage revenue - variable COGS - credits cost) / Usage revenue
   - Variable COGS inputs: GPU cost model from FP&A, cache hit attribution assumptions (must be explicitly stated), and model mix.
   - Reporting: margin by segment (model family + region) and an overall blended number.

### Secondary metrics (required unless explicitly waived)
- **ARPA/ARPU** (per active account) over 30 days
- **Support burden**: billing-related tickets per 1k active accounts + dispute rate
- **Usage distribution**: p50/p90 spend per account + free-tier exhaustion distribution
- **Churn proxy** (30 day): % accounts with 0 usage days in days 21–30 after being active in days 1–10

### Guardrail metrics (stop immediately if breached)
- **Invoice dispute rate**: >0.5% of invoiced accounts opening billing disputes in a 7-day window (or >2 disputes/day for smaller cohorts)
- **Metering anomaly indicators**: drift vs ledger above thresholds from PM-1842 (flag as “data invalid”; pause analysis)
- **Gross margin floor**: blended contribution margin drops below Finance-approved floor for experiment segment (default: -3 pts vs control for >7 days)
- **Activation regression**: >10% relative drop in first-week activation (accounts with >=1 successful request) vs control

## Stop / continue criteria (standard)
### Minimum runtime (to reduce premature decisions)
- Minimum 14 days for conversion metrics, unless guardrails triggered.
- Minimum 30 days for retention proxy; 60 days for early NRR.

### Minimum sample size / power (v1 pragmatic rule)
- Do not declare “wins” until either:
  - 500 exposed new signups per arm for self-serve conversion experiments, OR
  - 200 active accounts per arm for retention/margin experiments,
  AND at least 2 full billing cycles worth of usage events have landed (consider late-arriving events).
- If traffic is lower, require Sana to provide a power note (MDE + confidence) and recommend extending/terminating.

### Decision thresholds (default)
- **Scale** if:
  - Conversion +5% relative or greater vs control (14-day), AND
  - Margin non-inferiority within -1 pt blended vs control (or better), AND
  - No guardrail breaches.
- **Stop** if:
  - Conversion -5% relative or worse for 7 consecutive days after day 7, OR
  - Margin -3 pts blended vs control for 7 consecutive days, OR
  - Support/billing disputes exceed guardrail.
- **Continue** if mixed: propose explicit next-step hypothesis and what signal we’re waiting for (e.g., margin improves after behavior stabilizes).

## Metering-change caveat (mandatory in every readout)
Because metering fixes are landing during Q1, every analysis MUST segment:
- **Pre-meter-fix window** and **post-meter-fix window** (using the “meter_version” / deployment marker from Telemetry).
- If meter_version is not available in the dataset, analysis must be blocked until Eng provides a joinable marker.
- Any readout that mixes windows must be labeled “directional only” and cannot be used for pricing decisions.

## Data sources (source of truth)
- Revenue + credits: billing ledger (Finance-controlled table/export)
- Usage: usage events with billed token fields (not raw tokens) once available
- Cohort exposure: experiment flag + cohort tagging events (RevOps/analytics)
- Costs: FP&A variable COGS model inputs (Rishi)

If there is disagreement between usage exports and ledger, ledger wins for revenue reporting; usage events are used for diagnostics only until reconciled.

## Approval workflow
### A) Before launch
1. PM/ProdOps drafts experiment plan with metrics + guardrails using this standard.
2. Finance review (Rishi + Emily): confirms margin methodology + credit handling.
3. Legal review only if customer-facing copy changes (separate ticket).
4. Final go/no-go: Evelyn (CPO) + Laura (CFO) for experiments that impact pricing page or default plan.

### B) Before increasing rollout %
- Required checkpoint: updated interim dashboard + anomaly check
- Sign-off: Chris (Product Ops) + Rishi (FP&A) + Logan/Nadia for metering stability note

### C) After conclusion
- Final readout includes: decision, risks, rollout plan, and “meter caveat” section.
- Finance signs off on RevRec implications and whether any credits/adjustments are needed (usually forward-only).

## Open questions
1) Confirm default margin floor thresholds by segment (self-serve vs sales-led). (Owner: Rishi)
2) Confirm conversion definition when paywall is “card required” vs “spend threshold”. (Owner: Nikhil)
3) Decide whether we standardize on Bayesian vs frequentist reporting in readouts (v1: pragmatic thresholds + directional CI). (Owner: Sana)

## Links / related work
- Pricing experiment analysis plan (Drive): shared_drives/product/product-ops/pricing-experiment-analysis-plan-2026q1
- Cohort definitions (Drive): shared_drives/product/hosted-api/experiment-vs-control-cohort-definitions
- Meter sanity KPIs (Linear): PM-1842
- Meter change control (Linear): PM-1872

## Acceptance criteria
- A single doc (linked from experiment overview) that defines metrics + stop criteria, with a readout template.
- Finance-approved thresholds and explicit credit handling guidance.
- Used in the next experiment stop/continue decision meeting; any deviations must be called out explicitly in the readout.

2026-02-18 (Nikhil Sharma): Please add clarity on “paid conversion” for card-required variants vs usage-threshold variants. Also add a standard activation metric so we catch top-of-funnel regressions.
